question: Rutherford’s α-particle scattering experiment led to the discovery of which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiment** was conducted in **1911** to study the structure of the atom. The experiment used **alpha particles** directed at a thin sheet of gold foil.
 
• Most of the alpha particles passed through the foil without any deflection, indicating that most of the atom consists of **empty space**.
 
• However, a small fraction of particles were deflected at large angles, and a very few even bounced back. This led to the conclusion that the atom contains a **dense, positively charged core**, which Rutherford named the **nucleus**.
 
• The nucleus was found to occupy a very small volume compared to the overall size of the atom, but it contains most of the atom's **mass**.
 
• This experiment laid the foundation for the **planetary model of the atom**, where electrons orbit around the nucleus, similar to planets orbiting the Sun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Atom:**

 
 
• An atom consists of three subatomic particles: **protons**, **neutrons**, and **electrons**.
 
• The **protons** and **neutrons** are located in the **nucleus**, while the **electrons** orbit around the nucleus in defined energy levels or shells.
 
• The **nucleus** is positively charged due to the presence of protons, while electrons carry a negative charge.
 
• The discovery of the nucleus helped in understanding the **mass and charge distribution** within an atom.
 
 
 
• **Key Findings of Rutherford’s Experiment:**
 
 
• Most of the atom's volume is **empty space**, as most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without deflection.
 
• The positive charge and most of the mass of the atom are concentrated in a very small region called the **nucleus**.
 
• The nucleus is extremely small compared to the overall size of the atom, with a diameter of approximately **10^-15 meters**.
 
• Electrons occupy the space surrounding the nucleus, forming the **electron cloud**.
 
 
 
• **Other Models of the Atom:**
 
 
• **Thomson’s Model (1897):** Proposed the "plum pudding" model where electrons were embedded in a positively charged sphere.
 
• **Bohr’s Model (1913):** Improved upon Rutherford’s model by introducing quantized energy levels for electrons.
 
• **Quantum Mechanical Model:** The modern atomic theory based on quantum mechanics, which describes electrons as existing in probabilistic regions called **orbitals**.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics of Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• **Protons:** Positively charged, found in the nucleus, mass = 1.6726 × 10^-27 kg.
 
• **Neutrons:** Neutral, found in the nucleus, mass = 1.675 × 10^-27 kg.
 
• **Electrons:** Negatively charged, orbit around the nucleus, mass = 9.109 × 10^-31 kg.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alpha Particles:** Alpha particles are helium nuclei, consisting of **two protons and two neutrons**. They are positively charged and were used in Rutherford’s experiment to probe the structure of the atom.
 
• **Gold Foil:** The thin gold foil used in the experiment was approximately **0.00004 cm thick**, allowing alpha particles to pass through it while interacting with the atomic structure.
 
• **Deflection Observations:** Large-angle deflections indicated the presence of a dense, positively charged nucleus, while straight-line paths indicated empty space in the atom.
 
• **Impact on Modern Physics:** Rutherford’s findings revolutionized atomic theory, paving the way for further discoveries such as **Bohr’s quantized energy levels** and the development of quantum mechanics.
